title: Luminescent materials based on aromatic bisimides—part 1: the smaller pyromellitic and naphthalene derivatives
content: In this review, we have gathered insights into the advancements in the development and application of small aromatic bis(dicarboximide) compounds, with a particular focus on their fluorescence, thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), room temperature phosphorescence (RTP), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) properties. Traditionally, a low fluorescence quantum yield (QY), which is characteristic of the parent pyromellitic and naphthalene bisimides, has been viewed as a disadvantage for optoelectronic applications. However, emerging research highlighted in this review indicates that these properties can actually be beneficial due to the efficient harvesting of triplet excitons. This can be achieved in several ways, such as embedding aromatic bisimides in rigid polymeric or supramolecular matrices, utilizing the heavy-atom effect, or through tailored charge-transfer (CT) complexation with electron-rich (hetero-)aromatics. As a result, recent studies on small aromatic bisimides have established them as an important class of functional materials for generating photoluminescence across a wide spectral range and for applications in photocatalysis.
